decisions.decision: No new Iceberg tables — query/validation module only
decisions.rationale: The base-financial-facts-model spec already built the correct schema with all bitemporal fields. This spec adds the ergonomic layer: query helpers, snapshot management, and temporal DQ rules. Adding tables would duplicate data.

decisions.decision: as_known_on uses filed_date, not Iceberg snapshots
decisions.rationale: filed_date is the real-world 'when was this known?' signal (valid time). Iceberg snapshot time is system-level transaction time — it reflects when data was loaded into the pipeline, not when the SEC received the filing. For 'what did we know on date X?' the filing date is authoritative.
Matches the existing base zone pattern established in financial_facts_model. Keeps functions testable without Iceberg infrastructure. Only facts_at_snapshot requires an Iceberg table reference.

decisions.decision: Snapshot registry is in-memory, not a new table
decisions.rationale: Storing snapshot metadata in an Iceberg table would be circular — the registry would need its own snapshots. The in-memory approach enriches PyIceberg's get_snapshots() with labels and ISO timestamps on the fly.
Single source of truth for the grain definition. If the grain changes, it changes in one place. Clean dependency — bitemporal module depends on financial_facts_model config, not the other way around.

Some SEC filings have edge cases where filed_date is before end_date (e.g., NT filings, early preliminary filings). A 100% threshold would produce false failures. 99% allows for known edge cases while still catching systemic issues.
